name: Kolka–Karmadon rock/ice avalanche, Kazbek massif, North Ossetia, Russia
notes: Huggel et al. (2005) characterise the event as a slope failure that entrained Kolka Glacier and describe two flow phases; Kääb et al. (2021) classify it as a low-angle glacier detachment, which is the failure_type used here. dammed_river / secondary_surge are non-nullable booleans in the contract; where the retrieved sources do not state them they are recorded as false, meaning 'not established in the retrieved text', not 'established absent'.

estimates.qualifier: avalanche 'traveled down the Genaldon valley for 20km' to the Karmadon gorge
additional distal mudflow that 'continued for another 15km' beyond the gorge (not included in low/high)

runout_km.notes: low/high cover the avalanche reach only; Huggel et al. describe a further 15 km distal mudflow

source_location.basis: Kolka Glacier location as listed in Table 1 of Kääb et al. (2021), stated to 0.01°

source_volume_m3.notes: Two peer-reviewed figures differ by 30 %; no best is chosen

sources.excerpt: traveled down the Genaldon valley for 20km, was stopped at the entrance of the Karmadon gorge, and was finally succeeded by a distal mudflow which continued for another 15km. The event caused the death of ca. 140 people
sources.title: The 2002 rock/ice avalanche at Kolka/Karmadon, Russian Caucasus: assessment of extraordinary avalanche formation and mobility, and application of QuickBird satellite imagery

sources.excerpt: The detachment of Kolka Glacier on 20 September 2002 released 130×10 6 m 3 of ice and rock that claimed ∼ 135 lives
sources.title: Sudden large-volume detachments of low-angle mountain glaciers – more frequent than thought?
